newsitem.title: UK: UK March bank mortgage lending rises 755 mln stg.
newsitem.headline: UK March bank mortgage lending rises 755 mln stg.

text.p: Net lending to house buyers by Britain's major banks rose by a seaonally adjusted 775 million stg in March, following a 780 million increase in February, the British Bankers' Association said on Monday.
Unadjusted gross loans totalled 2.175 billion stg, just one percent up on February's 2.153 billion figure.
The number of new mortgage approvals rose to 39,642 in March from 34,529 the month before -- an increase of 15 percent.
In value terms, new approvals increased by 17 percent, to 2.312 billion stg from 1.984 billion.

"Continuing the pattern for the year, the major banks' mortgage business was again fairly strong, with net lending some 10 percent above the recent monthly average," said Tim Sweeney, the BBA's director-general.
He said for the first three months of the year, net mortgage lending was about 16 percent higher than in the last quarter of 1996.
But the rise in the number and value of new approvals was less than expected for the time of year. In March last year, gross lending rose by nearly 20 percent from the month before.
"It may be that overall demand for mortgage finance has been restrained somewhat by concerns over future interest rate movements and uncertainties related to the election," Sweeney said.

"It is possible also that a shortage of property in certain areas has had some effect in dampening the growth in mortgage lending," he added. "In any event, prospects for incomes growth suggest a continuation of sustained housing market recovery."
